Suppose that $A$ is an $n\times n$ matrix.

Assuming that $\vvec$ is an eigenvector of $A$ whose associated eigenvalue is nonzero, explain why $\vvec$ is in $\col(A)$.

Assuming that $\vvec$ is an eigenvector of $A$ whose associated eigenvalue is zero, explain why $\vvec$ is in $\nul(A)$.

Consider the two special matrices below and find their eigenvectors and associated eigenvalues. $$ A = \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp 1 \amp 1 \\ 1 \amp 1 \amp 1 \\ 1 \amp 1 \amp 1 \\ \end{array}\right],~~~ B = \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp 1 \amp 1 \\ 2 \amp 2 \amp 2 \\ 3 \amp 3 \amp 3 \\ \end{array}\right]. $$
